native_mcp_support.notes: Anthropic created and maintains the MCP specification. The Claude API exposes a first-party MCP connector (beta header mcp-client-2025-11-20; the older mcp-client-2025-04-04 is deprecated) that attaches remote MCP servers directly to a Messages request. CHANGE vs 2026-06-21: supported platforms are now the Claude API, Claude Platform on AWS AND Microsoft Foundry (Hosted-on-Anthropic deployments), all in beta; Amazon Bedrock and Google Cloud are still not listed. Transports: Streamable HTTP and SSE — local stdio servers cannot be attached through the connector. Of the MCP feature set only tool calls are supported; prompts and resources are not.

skills_concept.value: Agent Skills — modular, filesystem-based capability bundles (SKILL.md + optional scripts/resources) loaded by three-level progressive disclosure: Level 1 metadata (~100 tokens/skill) always in the system prompt; Level 2 instructions (under 5k tokens) loaded on demand when the skill triggers; Level 3+ bundled files read only when needed, with scripts run through bash so only their output enters context.
skills_concept.notes: Documented field limits: name max 64 characters (lowercase letters, digits, hyphens; no XML tags; may not contain "anthropic" or "claude"); description non-empty, max 1024 characters. Anthropic states you "can install many Skills without context penalty: until a Skill is triggered, only its name and description occupy context" and documents no numeric ceiling on how many Skills may be installed; what binds is the context window -- every installed Skill keeps its name and description in context, and its full instructions load into context on invocation. Available on the Claude API, claude.ai, Claude Code (custom Skills only — pre-built document Skills are not available there), Claude Platform on AWS and Microsoft Foundry (pre-built Skills require a Hosted-on-Anthropic deployment).

context_window_tokens.notes: 1M-token context window on the Claude API, Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud and Microsoft Foundry. "For every model with a 1M-token context window, 1M is the default: you don't need a beta header, and long-context requests are billed at standard pricing." Note the deployment caveat: Claude Code documents that Opus-family and Sonnet 5 sessions can be budgeted at 200K on Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform and Microsoft Foundry, and CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_1M_CONTEXT=1 holds native-1M models to 200K.

input_output_shared.notes: One shared pool: system prompt, all prior messages, tool definitions, the current user message and the response Claude generates (including its thinking) all count toward the window.

max_input_tokens.notes: Derived: context window (1,000,000) minus max output (128,000). Anthropic publishes no separate static max-input number in prose. The practical ceiling is lower once the tool-use system prompt, tool definitions and Skill metadata are counted.

max_output_tokens_default.notes: "A single request to any model with a 1M-token context window can generate up to 128k output tokens (max_tokens)."

max_output_tokens_max.notes: 128k is both the synchronous and the batch ceiling for this model: the output-300k-2026-03-24 extended-output beta lists only Opus 5, Opus 4.8, Opus 4.7, Opus 4.6, Sonnet 5 and Sonnet 4.6 — Fable 5 and Mythos 5 are not included.

extended_context.notes: No separate extended-context beta applies: 1M is the GA default window and is billed at standard per-token pricing ("Claude 4.6 and later models and Claude Mythos Preview include the full 1M token context window at standard pricing").

reasoning_tokens_count_as_output.notes: Thinking tokens are a subset of max_tokens, count toward the context window and rate limits, and are billed as output. IMPORTANT CHANGE vs the 2026-06-21 snapshot: this model KEEPS previous-turn thinking blocks — "On models that strip previous thinking blocks (Claude Opus <4.5, Claude Sonnet <4.6, all Haiku), thinking blocks generated in one turn don't carry forward... On newer models (Opus 4.5+, Sonnet 4.6+, Fable 5, Mythos 5), thinking blocks are kept and count as input tokens in subsequent turns." Use context editing to clear them if the growth is unwanted.

tokenizer_family.notes: Proprietary BPE; not cl100k or o200k. This model uses the newer tokenizer: "Claude 4.7 and later models and Claude Mythos Preview use a newer tokenizer that contributes to their improved performance on a wide range of tasks. This tokenizer produces approximately 30% more tokens for the same text... Claude Sonnet 4.6 and earlier models use the previous tokenizer." (The 2026-06-21 snapshot recorded 35%; the current figure is 30%.)

tokenizer_public.notes: Anthropic has not released tokenizer weights or a public BPE vocabulary. Exact counts require the count_tokens endpoint. Token counting is free, subject to separate RPM limits (Start 2,000 / Build 4,000 / Scale 8,000 RPM), and "all active models support token counting, including Claude Opus 5 and Claude Sonnet 5".

tokenizer_access.notes: POST /v1/messages/count_tokens. Accepts the same structured inputs as /v1/messages — system prompts, tools, images, PDFs, and thinking blocks (current-turn thinking counts; previous-turn thinking is ignored). Free, rate-limited separately from message creation. The returned count is an estimate and may differ slightly from billed tokens; system-added tokens are counted but never billed.

count_tokens_method.notes: Returns {input_tokens: N} and includes the serialized tools array, so it is the correct way to measure an MCP server's startup footprint for this model. Always pass the specific model — tokenizer generations differ across Claude models.

image_token_rule.value: ceil(width/28) x ceil(height/28) visual tokens per image; high-resolution tier — max 2576px long edge, max 4784 visual tokens. Images are billed at the model's input token rate.
image_token_rule.notes: Resolution tier table: "High-resolution | Claude 4.7 and later models | 2576 px | 4784". This model is later than Claude 4.7 so it falls in the high-resolution tier; the vision page names Claude Opus 5 explicitly but does not enumerate every 4.7+ model, so the tier assignment for the other 4.7+ models is read off the version rule rather than a per-model row — hence medium confidence. Images are padded to the next multiple of 28px. A single request may carry up to 600 images or PDF pages on a 1M-window model (100 on a 200k-window model).

audio_token_rule.notes: Audio input is not a supported modality on any current Claude model as of 2026-08-19; the models comparison lists text, image and PDF (vision) only. Recorded as null (undocumented/unsupported), not as a limit value.

chars_per_token_estimate.notes: Derived: Anthropic's glossary states "a token approximately represents 3.5 English characters"; the newer tokenizer used by Claude 4.7+ produces ~30% more tokens for the same text, giving 3.5 / 1.30 = ~2.7 chars/token. Using the pricing page's coarser "1 token is approximately 4 characters" instead yields ~3.1. The two vendor pages conflict on the base figure (3.5 vs 4); treat 2.7-3.1 as the band and use count_tokens for anything that matters. Rough fallback for raw_json_rough only.

function_calling.notes: Tool use is supported through the tools[] parameter on the Messages API; Claude 4 and later models emit parallel tool calls by default.

native_mcp.notes: MCP connector (beta header mcp-client-2025-11-20) on the Claude API, Claude Platform on AWS and Microsoft Foundry (Hosted on Anthropic). Remote Streamable-HTTP/SSE servers only; tool calls only from the MCP spec.

parallel_tool_calls.notes: "Claude 4 and later models make parallel tool calls by default when a request benefits from multiple tools." A single assistant turn can contain several tool_use blocks.

max_tools_hard.notes: No API-enforced numeric cap on the number of tools accepted per request is published (unlike OpenAI's 128-tool cap). The limits that DO bind are: the documented AGGREGATE catalog ceiling of 10,000 tools with defer_loading (see max_total_tools), the documented selection cliff — Anthropic states "Claude's ability to pick the right tool degrades once you exceed 30-50 available tools" — the 1M/200k context window the serialized tool JSON is billed into, and the 32 MB request payload limit. Scope: aggregate (all connected MCP servers + built-in tools in one request), not per server.

max_tools_practical.notes: Anthropic's tool-search doc states verbatim: "Claude's ability to pick the right tool degrades once you exceed 30-50 available tools." 40 is the midpoint of that documented band. Scope: aggregate across all servers. EMPIRICAL guidance, not an enforced spec value — vendor-published but behavioural, so confidence is medium. With tool search / defer_loading the usable catalog extends to the 10,000-tool aggregate ceiling.

tool_definition_shape.notes: Tools are {name, description, input_schema} in the tools[] array; name must match ^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{1,64}$. Definitions are serialized into an API-injected tool-use system prompt. MCP tools arrive as mcp_toolset objects and are counted identically as input tokens.

tool_defs_count_as_input.notes: Tool names, descriptions and input schemas in the tools parameter are billed as input tokens. Fable 5 is NOT listed in the per-model tool-use system prompt overhead table on the tool-use overview page as of 2026-08-19, so the fixed injected overhead for this model is undocumented (Opus 5 is 286/406 tokens for auto|none / any|tool; Opus 4.8 is 290/410).

tool_search_deferral.notes: Listed first in the tool search model-compatibility table with both tool_search_tool_regex_20251119 and tool_search_tool_bm25_20251119. defer_loading keeps a tool out of the system prompt until Claude discovers it; typical context saving is over 85%.

max_tool_name_len.notes: "Must match the regex ^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{1,64}$." MCP client namespacing (server prefix + tool name) eats into this budget. Agent Skill names have a separate 64-character limit.

max_tool_description_len.notes: No character or token cap on tool description length is documented as of 2026-08-19. Anthropic's guidance is the opposite direction — "Aim for at least 3-4 sentences for each tool description, more if the tool is complex." Descriptions are billed as input tokens, so the binding ceilings are the context window and the 32 MB request payload limit.

max_request_size.notes: Direct Claude API: 32 MB for Messages and Token Counting (also Sessions/Agents/Environments); Message Batches API 256 MB; Files API 500 MB. Exceeding returns 413 request_too_large. Partner platforms differ: Amazon Bedrock 20 MB, Google Cloud 30 MB; Claude Platform on AWS uses the same limits as the direct API. Tool definitions count toward this payload AND toward the context window — two separate ceilings.

max_tool_result_size.notes: No per-tool-result byte or token cap is documented at the model-API layer; tool_result content blocks are billed as input tokens and are bounded by the 32 MB request limit and the context window. The documented cap that DOES bind sits at the client layer: Claude Code warns when an MCP tool result exceeds 10,000 tokens and truncates at 25,000 tokens by default (MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS; a server may override per tool with the anthropic/maxResultSizeChars annotation). Programmatic tool calling is the other lever — results of tools called from inside the code-execution container do not enter the model's context at all.

max_parallel_tool_calls_count.notes: Parallel tool use is supported — an assistant turn can contain several tool_use blocks — but no numeric cap on simultaneous calls per turn is published. Bounded in practice by the turn's output-token budget. tool_choice.disable_parallel_tool_use:true forces at most one tool call per response (exactly one when tool_choice is any/tool).

tool_use_per_turn_limit.notes: No per-turn tool-call-cycle cap is published in the Messages API docs. The controls that DO bound an agentic turn are: max_tokens (hard — truncates with stop_reason max_tokens), task budgets (beta, advisory soft hint, minimum 20,000 tokens, Opus 5 / Fable 5 / Mythos 5 / Opus 4.8 / Opus 4.7 only), and tool_choice.disable_parallel_tool_use, which restricts a turn to at most one tool call.

max_connected_servers.notes: No numeric cap on the mcp_servers array per request is documented for the MCP connector; the connector only requires that each mcp_server_name is referenced by exactly one mcp_toolset. At the client layer Claude Code states it "can connect to hundreds of external tools and data sources" and that it "doesn't impose a fixed per-server tool cap; the practical limit is your context window budget". The binding constraints are therefore the aggregate tool budget and the window, not a server count.

max_total_tools.notes: AGGREGATE ceiling across ALL connected MCP servers + built-in tools in one request (NOT a per-server cap), and conditional on tool search / defer_loading: "Maximum deferred tools: 10,000 tools with defer_loading: true per request". Without defer_loading the binding constraint is the documented 30-50 tool selection cliff plus the context window. Anthropic's own example: a 5-server setup (GitHub, Slack, Sentry, Grafana, Splunk) costs ~55k tokens in definitions before any work; tool search cuts that by over 85%.

tools_mcp.tool_schema_limits_notes: Tools are {name, description, input_schema (JSON Schema)} with optional input_examples, cache_control, strict, defer_loading, allowed_callers and eager_input_streaming. Structured outputs / strict tool use share one documented JSON Schema restriction: pattern (regex) is NOT supported — the Python, TypeScript, Ruby and PHP SDKs strip unsupported keywords and fold them into field descriptions. No documented maximum nesting depth, maximum property count, maximum enum size or maximum total schema size. strict is available on all tools except mcp_toolset; defer_loading is available on all tools (per-tool or per-toolset for MCP). input_examples cost ~20-50 tokens for simple examples and ~100-200 tokens for complex nested objects, and are not available on server tools. Tool definitions can carry cache_control, so a repeated tool array reads at 0.1x input price after a cache write; deferred tools sit outside the system-prompt prefix so defer_loading preserves the cached prefix and composes with strict mode without grammar recompilation. Programmatic tool calling is the largest schema-adjacent lever here: results of tools invoked from inside the code-execution container do not count toward input/output tokens at all — Anthropic measured roughly 38% fewer billed input tokens on a 75-tool project-management agent benchmark with no accuracy change.
tools_mcp.other_limits_notes: MCP connector (API layer, beta header mcp-client-2025-11-20; mcp-client-2025-04-04 is deprecated): HTTPS remote servers only over Streamable HTTP or SSE — local stdio servers cannot be attached directly. Of the MCP specification only tool calls are supported; prompts and resources are not. Available on the Claude API, Claude Platform on AWS and Microsoft Foundry (Hosted-on-Anthropic deployments), all in beta. Per-tool mcp_toolset config exposes enabled and defer_loading (default false). Tool search regex variant: max 200-character pattern; error_code values are invalid_tool_input, unavailable, too_many_requests and execution_time_exceeded. Request size 32 MB direct / 20 MB Bedrock / 30 MB Google Cloud. A single request may carry up to 600 images or PDF pages on 1M-window models (100 on 200k-window models). Fable 5 additionally supports programmatic tool calling (code_execution_20260120), task budgets (beta, task-budgets-2026-03-13, minimum 20,000 tokens, advisory not enforced), the memory tool, tool result clearing through context editing, compaction, and mid-conversation tool changes (beta, mid-conversation-tool-changes-2026-07-01, which lets you change the tools array mid-conversation without invalidating the prompt cache). Thinking is always on: thinking:{"type":"disabled"} is rejected, and the raw chain of thought is never returned (thinking.display is "omitted" by default or "summarized"). Safety classifiers may decline a request, returning stop_reason:"refusal" as an HTTP 200; an opt-in fallbacks parameter can re-run refused requests on another model at that model's rates. Fable 5 carries 30-day data retention and is not available under zero data retention.

strict_function_schema.notes: No OpenAI-style strict function-schema mode that enforces 100-prop / 5-depth / no-oneOf. Anthropic does ship a strict flag (strict:true, plus structured outputs) but its documented rule set is different and looser: the only keyword restriction published is that pattern (regex) is unsupported, and no property-count or depth ceiling is given. Captured in tool_schema_limits_notes.

skills_loading_model.notes: Level 1 metadata (name + description from YAML frontmatter, ~100 tokens per Skill) is always in context at startup. Level 2 (SKILL.md body, under 5k tokens) loads only when the Skill triggers. Level 3+ bundled files load only when read; scripts run through bash so only their output enters context. Documented field limits: name max 64 characters (lowercase letters, numbers, hyphens; no XML tags; may not contain "anthropic" or "claude"), description non-empty and max 1024 characters.

skills_context.skills_context_cost_notes: ~100 tokens per installed Skill at startup (Level 1 name+description). When a Skill triggers, its SKILL.md body adds under 5k tokens (Level 2). Level 3 bundled files cost nothing until read; scripts execute through bash so only stdout/stderr enters context. Anthropic states you "can install many Skills without context penalty: until a Skill is triggered, only its name and description occupy context", and documents no numeric ceiling on the number of installed Skills; the binding limit is the context window -- each installed Skill holds its name and description in context, and its full instructions load on invocation.
skills_context.system_prompt_overhead_notes: Fable 5 is not listed in the tool-use system prompt overhead table as of 2026-08-19, so the fixed injected tool-use system prompt cost is undocumented for this model. For orientation, the neighbouring frontier models are Opus 5 at 286 tokens (tool_choice auto/none) / 406 (any/tool) and Opus 4.8 at 290/410. System-added tokens are counted by count_tokens but are not billed.

prompt_caching.notes: Supported on all active Claude models, automatic and explicit. Multipliers: 5-minute cache write 1.25x base input, 1-hour cache write 2x, cache read (hit) 0.1x. For Claude Fable 5 that is $12.5/MTok (5m write), $20.0/MTok (1h write) and $1.0/MTok (read) against a $10.0/MTok base. Minimum cacheable prompt length: 512 tokens. cache_control can be set on tool definitions and on an mcp_toolset, so a stable MCP tool array is cacheable; deferred tools sit outside the cached system-prompt prefix and do not invalidate it.

memory_feature.notes: First-party memory tool (memory_20250818), generally available on the Messages API with no beta header, on "all Claude 4 and later models". Operates as just-in-time retrieval: Claude checks its memory directory and reads files back on demand, so retrieved content enters the window as ordinary input tokens rather than a permanent always-on block. Anthropic does not publish a token accounting rule for memory content.

cached_input_per_mtok_usd.notes: Cache read (hit) = 0.1x base input. 5-minute cache write = 1.25x, 1-hour cache write = 2x.

batch_discount.notes: Message Batches API: $5.0/MTok input, $25.0/MTok output for Claude Fable 5. Batch and prompt-caching discounts stack, and both apply at standard rates across the full context window.

cost.multimodal_billing_notes: Images are billed as input tokens at the visual-token rate (high-resolution tier, max 4784 tokens/image). No separate per-image fee; PDFs are treated the same way. Audio is not supported. Server tools can add per-use charges. Fast mode is not offered for Fable 5 (only Opus 5 and Opus 4.8).

reasoning_billed_as_output.notes: Thinking tokens count toward the context window, count toward rate limits, are a subset of max_tokens, and are billed at the output rate ($50.0/MTok here).

models.notes: Claude Fable 5 is Anthropic's most capable widely released model, launched 2026-06-09 alongside the restricted Claude Mythos 5 and built for demanding reasoning and long-horizon agentic work. Adaptive thinking is always on and cannot be disabled; effort is the control for thinking depth. It sits ABOVE Opus 5 on price ($10/$50 vs $5/$25). Availability was withdrawn 2026-06-12 under US export controls and restored 2026-07-01 (source: https://www.anthropic.com/news/redeploying-fable-5). Deprecation table: Active, tentative retirement not sooner than 2027-06-09. Uses the newer (4.7+) tokenizer. Not covered by the 300k batch-output beta, and absent from the tool-use system prompt overhead table.

Tool definitions count toward this payload AND toward the context window — two separate ceilings.

max_tool_result_size.notes: No per-tool-result byte or token cap is documented at the model-API layer; tool_result content blocks are billed as input tokens and are bounded by the 32 MB request limit and the context window. The documented cap that DOES bind sits at the client layer: Claude Code warns when an MCP tool result exceeds 10,000 tokens and truncates at 25,000 tokens by default (MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS; a server may override per tool with the anthropic/maxResultSizeChars annotation). Programmatic tool calling is the other lever — results of tools called from inside the code-execution container do not enter the model's context at all.

max_parallel_tool_calls_count.notes: Parallel tool use is supported — an assistant turn can contain several tool_use blocks — but no numeric cap on simultaneous calls per turn is published. Bounded in practice by the turn's output-token budget. tool_choice.disable_parallel_tool_use:true forces at most one tool call per response (exactly one when tool_choice is any/tool).

tool_use_per_turn_limit.notes: No per-turn tool-call-cycle cap is published in the Messages API docs. The controls that DO bound an agentic turn are: max_tokens (hard — truncates with stop_reason max_tokens), task budgets (beta, advisory soft hint, minimum 20,000 tokens, Opus 5 / Fable 5 / Mythos 5 / Opus 4.8 / Opus 4.7 only), and tool_choice.disable_parallel_tool_use, which restricts a turn to at most one tool call.

max_connected_servers.notes: No numeric cap on the mcp_servers array per request is documented for the MCP connector; the connector only requires that each mcp_server_name is referenced by exactly one mcp_toolset. At the client layer Claude Code states it "can connect to hundreds of external tools and data sources" and that it "doesn't impose a fixed per-server tool cap; the practical limit is your context window budget". The binding constraints are therefore the aggregate tool budget and the window, not a server count.

max_total_tools.notes: AGGREGATE ceiling across ALL connected MCP servers + built-in tools in one request (NOT a per-server cap), and conditional on tool search / defer_loading: "Maximum deferred tools: 10,000 tools with defer_loading: true per request". Without defer_loading the binding constraint is the documented 30-50 tool selection cliff plus the context window. Anthropic's own example: a 5-server setup (GitHub, Slack, Sentry, Grafana, Splunk) costs ~55k tokens in definitions before any work; tool search cuts that by over 85%.

tools_mcp.tool_schema_limits_notes: Tools are {name, description, input_schema (JSON Schema)} with optional input_examples, cache_control, strict, defer_loading, allowed_callers and eager_input_streaming. Structured outputs / strict tool use share one documented JSON Schema restriction: pattern (regex) is NOT supported — the Python, TypeScript, Ruby and PHP SDKs strip unsupported keywords and fold them into field descriptions. No documented maximum nesting depth, maximum property count, maximum enum size or maximum total schema size. strict is available on all tools except mcp_toolset; defer_loading is available on all tools (per-tool or per-toolset for MCP). input_examples cost ~20-50 tokens for simple examples and ~100-200 tokens for complex nested objects, and are not available on server tools. Tool definitions can carry cache_control, so a repeated tool array reads at 0.1x input price after a cache write; deferred tools sit outside the system-prompt prefix so defer_loading preserves the cached prefix and composes with strict mode without grammar recompilation.
tools_mcp.other_limits_notes: MCP connector (API layer, beta header mcp-client-2025-11-20; mcp-client-2025-04-04 is deprecated): HTTPS remote servers only over Streamable HTTP or SSE — local stdio servers cannot be attached directly. Per-tool mcp_toolset config exposes enabled and defer_loading (default false). Request size 32 MB direct / 20 MB Bedrock / 30 MB Google Cloud. A single request may carry up to 600 images or PDF pages on 1M-window models (100 on 200k-window models). Mythos 5 supports programmatic tool calling, task budgets (beta), the memory tool, code execution, tool result clearing through context editing, compaction, vision, and mid-conversation tool changes (beta). Thinking is always on (thinking:{"type":"disabled"} is rejected) and the raw chain of thought is never returned. The defining difference from Fable 5: Mythos 5 does NOT run the safety classifiers, so it does not produce stop_reason:"refusal". 30-day data retention; no zero-data-retention option.

strict_function_schema.notes: No OpenAI-style strict function-schema mode that enforces 100-prop / 5-depth / no-oneOf. tools_mcp.tool_schema_limits_notes: Tools are {name, description, input_schema (JSON Schema)} with optional input_examples, cache_control, strict, defer_loading, allowed_callers and eager_input_streaming. No documented maximum nesting depth, maximum property count, maximum enum size or maximum total schema size. strict is available on all tools except mcp_toolset; defer_loading is available on all tools (per-tool or per-toolset for MCP). input_examples cost ~20-50 tokens for simple examples and ~100-200 tokens for complex nested objects, and are not available on server tools. Tool definitions can carry cache_control, so a repeated tool array reads at 0.1x input price after a cache write; deferred tools sit outside the system-prompt prefix so defer_loading preserves the cached prefix and composes with strict mode without grammar recompilation. Programmatic tool calling applies here too: results of tools called from inside the code-execution container do not count toward input/output tokens (~38% fewer billed input tokens on Anthropic's 75-tool agent benchmark).
tools_mcp.other_limits_notes: MCP connector (API layer, beta header mcp-client-2025-11-20; mcp-client-2025-04-04 is deprecated): HTTPS remote servers only over Streamable HTTP or SSE — local stdio servers cannot be attached directly. Of the MCP specification only tool calls are supported; prompts and resources are not. Available on the Claude API, Claude Platform on AWS and Microsoft Foundry (Hosted-on-Anthropic deployments), all in beta. Per-tool mcp_toolset config exposes enabled and defer_loading (default false). Tool search regex variant: max 200-character pattern; error_code values are invalid_tool_input, unavailable, too_many_requests and execution_time_exceeded. Request size 32 MB direct / 20 MB Bedrock / 30 MB Google Cloud. A single request may carry up to 600 images or PDF pages on 1M-window models (100 on 200k-window models). Sonnet 5 supports programmatic tool calling (code_execution_20260120), structured outputs / strict tool use, the memory tool, context editing and compaction, and it receives the automatic context-awareness signals (a <budget:token_budget> tag at conversation start and a <system_warning> token usage line after each tool call). It does NOT support task budgets (beta) — those are Opus 5 / Fable 5 / Mythos 5 / Opus 4.8 / Opus 4.7 only — and it does not offer fast mode or Priority Tier. Migration breaking changes: adaptive thinking is on by default; manual extended thinking (thinking:{type:"enabled", budget_tokens:N}) is REMOVED and returns 400; non-default temperature / top_p / top_k return 400.

strict_function_schema.notes: No OpenAI-style strict function-schema mode that enforces 100-prop / 5-depth / no-oneOf. Anthropic does ship a strict flag (strict:true, plus structured outputs) but its documented rule set is different and looser: the only keyword restriction published is that pattern (regex) is unsupported, and no property-count or depth ceiling is given. Captured in tool_schema_limits_notes.

skills_supported.notes: Agent Skills available on the Claude API, claude.ai, Claude Code (custom Skills only), Claude Platform on AWS and Microsoft Foundry (pre-built Skills require a Hosted-on-Anthropic deployment).

skills_loading_model.notes: Level 1 metadata (name + description from YAML frontmatter, ~100 tokens per Skill) is always in context at startup. Level 2 (SKILL.md body, under 5k tokens) loads only when the Skill triggers. Level 3+ bundled files load only when read; scripts run through bash so only their output enters context. Documented field limits: name max 64 characters (lowercase letters, numbers, hyphens; no XML tags; may not contain "anthropic" or "claude"), description non-empty and max 1024 characters.

skills_context.skills_context_cost_notes: ~100 tokens per installed Skill at startup (Level 1 name+description). When a Skill triggers, its SKILL.md body adds under 5k tokens (Level 2). Level 3 bundled files cost nothing until read; scripts execute through bash so only stdout/stderr enters context. Anthropic states you "can install many Skills without context penalty: until a Skill is triggered, only its name and description occupy context", and documents no numeric ceiling on the number of installed Skills; the binding limit is the context window -- each installed Skill holds its name and description in context, and its full instructions load on invocation.

Context awareness is active on Sonnet 5: the API injects <budget:token_budget>N</budget:token_budget> at conversation start and a <system_warning>Token usage: X/N; Y remaining</system_warning> line after each tool call, so the model can self-manage a long MCP session. System-added tokens are counted but not billed.

prompt_caching.notes: Supported on all active Claude models, automatic and explicit. Multipliers: 5-minute cache write 1.25x base input, 1-hour cache write 2x, cache read (hit) 0.1x. For Claude Sonnet 5 that is $2.5/MTok (5m write), $4.0/MTok (1h write) and $0.2/MTok (read) against a $2.0/MTok base. Minimum cacheable prompt length: 1,024 tokens. cache_control can be set on tool definitions and on an mcp_toolset, so a stable MCP tool array is cacheable; deferred tools sit outside the cached system-prompt prefix and do not invalidate it.

memory_feature.notes: First-party memory tool (memory_20250818), generally available on the Messages API with no beta header, on "all Claude 4 and later models". Operates as just-in-time retrieval: Claude checks its memory directory and reads files back on demand, so retrieved content enters the window as ordinary input tokens rather than a permanent always-on block. Anthropic does not publish a token accounting rule for memory content.

cached_input_per_mtok_usd.notes: Cache read (hit) = 0.1x base input. 5-minute cache write = 1.25x, 1-hour cache write = 2x.

batch_discount.notes: Message Batches API: $1.0/MTok input, $5.0/MTok output for Claude Sonnet 5. Batch and prompt-caching discounts stack, and both apply at standard rates across the full context window.

cost.multimodal_billing_notes: Images billed as input tokens at the visual-token rate. PDFs the same; audio unsupported. Sonnet 5 is the cheapest 1M-window model in the roster at $2/$10 — the introductory price became permanent on 2026-08-10 (the planned rise to $3/$15 on 2026-09-01 was cancelled). No fast mode, no Priority Tier.

reasoning_billed_as_output.notes: Thinking tokens count toward the context window, count toward rate limits, are a subset of max_tokens, and are billed at the output rate ($10.0/MTok here).

models.notes: Claude Sonnet 5 (2026-06-30) supersedes Sonnet 4.6 as the default model on Free and Pro claude.ai plans and is the price/performance sweet spot of the roster: 1M context, 128k output, $2/$10 per MTok (permanent as of 2026-08-10). Adaptive thinking on by default; manual extended thinking and non-default sampling parameters now return 400. Effort levels standard / high / extra high. Newer (4.7+) tokenizer — Anthropic quantifies the shift as "roughly 1.0-1.35x depending on the content type" more tokens than Sonnet 4.6, so an MCP tool catalogue measured on Sonnet 4.6 will cost MORE tokens here despite the lower unit price. Available on the Claude API, AWS Bedrock and Microsoft Foundry; Google Vertex AI listed as coming soon. ADDED at the 2026-08-19 refresh.

function_calling.notes: Tool use is supported through the tools[] parameter on the Messages API; Claude 4 and later models emit parallel tool calls by default.

native_mcp.notes: MCP connector (beta header mcp-client-2025-11-20) on the Claude API, Claude Platform on AWS and Microsoft Foundry (Hosted on Anthropic). Remote Streamable-HTTP/SSE servers only; tool calls only.

parallel_tool_calls.notes: "Claude 4 and later models make parallel tool calls by default when a request benefits from multiple tools." A single assistant turn can contain several tool_use blocks.

max_tools_hard.notes: No API-enforced numeric cap on the number of tools accepted per request is published (unlike OpenAI's 128-tool cap). The limits that DO bind are: the documented AGGREGATE catalog ceiling of 10,000 tools with defer_loading (see max_total_tools), the documented selection cliff — Anthropic states "Claude's ability to pick the right tool degrades once you exceed 30-50 available tools" — the 1M/200k context window the serialized tool JSON is billed into, and the 32 MB request payload limit. Scope: aggregate (all connected MCP servers + built-in tools in one request), not per server.

max_tools_practical.notes: Anthropic documents the same 30-50 tool selection cliff for all models. 30 — the bottom of the documented band — is used for Haiku 4.5 because the 200k window is 5x smaller than the rest of the roster, so tool definitions cross a damaging share of the budget far sooner: Anthropic's own ~55k-token 5-server MCP example consumes 27.5% of Haiku's window versus 5.5% on a 1M model. EMPIRICAL, not an enforced spec value.

tool_definition_shape.notes: Tools are {name, description, input_schema} in the tools[] array; name must match ^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{1,64}$. Definitions are serialized into an API-injected tool-use system prompt. MCP tools arrive as mcp_toolset objects and are counted identically as input tokens.

tool_defs_count_as_input.notes: Tool definitions are billed as input tokens, plus an injected tool-use system prompt: Claude Haiku 4.5 costs 496 tokens with tool_choice auto|none and 588 tokens with any|tool (re-read 2026-08-19). On a 200k window that fixed overhead is ~0.3% of the budget before a single tool definition is counted.

tool_search_deferral.notes: Listed in the tool search model-compatibility table with both tool_search_tool_regex_20251119 and tool_search_tool_bm25_20251119. Claude Code names Haiku 4.5 as one of the models that support tool_reference blocks. Deferral matters most on this model: the smallest window in the roster makes upfront tool definitions the dominant context cost.

max_tool_name_len.notes: "Must match the regex ^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{1,64}$." MCP client namespacing (server prefix + tool name) eats into this budget. Agent Skill names have a separate 64-character limit.

max_tool_description_len.notes: No character or token cap on tool description length is documented as of 2026-08-19. Anthropic's guidance is the opposite direction — "Aim for at least 3-4 sentences for each tool description, more if the tool is complex." Descriptions are billed as input tokens, so the binding ceilings are the context window and the 32 MB request payload limit.

max_request_size.notes: Direct Claude API: 32 MB for Messages and Token Counting (also Sessions/Agents/Environments); Message Batches API 256 MB; Files API 500 MB. Exceeding returns 413 request_too_large. Partner platforms differ: Amazon Bedrock 20 MB, Google Cloud 30 MB; Claude Platform on AWS uses the same limits as the direct API. Tool definitions count toward this payload AND toward the context window — two separate ceilings.

max_tool_result_size.notes: No per-tool-result byte or token cap is documented at the model-API layer; tool_result content blocks are billed as input tokens and are bounded by the 32 MB request limit and the context window. The documented cap that DOES bind sits at the client layer: Claude Code warns when an MCP tool result exceeds 10,000 tokens and truncates at 25,000 tokens by default (MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS; a server may override per tool with the anthropic/maxResultSizeChars annotation). Programmatic tool calling is the other lever — results of tools called from inside the code-execution container do not enter the model's context at all.

max_parallel_tool_calls_count.notes: Parallel tool use is supported — an assistant turn can contain several tool_use blocks — but no numeric cap on simultaneous calls per turn is published. Bounded in practice by the turn's output-token budget. tool_choice.disable_parallel_tool_use:true forces at most one tool call per response (exactly one when tool_choice is any/tool).

tool_use_per_turn_limit.notes: No per-turn tool-call-cycle cap is published in the Messages API docs. The controls that DO bound an agentic turn are: max_tokens (hard — truncates with stop_reason max_tokens), task budgets (beta, advisory soft hint, minimum 20,000 tokens, Opus 5 / Fable 5 / Mythos 5 / Opus 4.8 / Opus 4.7 only), and tool_choice.disable_parallel_tool_use, which restricts a turn to at most one tool call.

max_connected_servers.notes: No numeric cap on the mcp_servers array per request is documented for the MCP connector; the connector only requires that each mcp_server_name is referenced by exactly one mcp_toolset. At the client layer Claude Code states it "can connect to hundreds of external tools and data sources" and that it "doesn't impose a fixed per-server tool cap; the practical limit is your context window budget". The binding constraints are therefore the aggregate tool budget and the window, not a server count.

max_total_tools.notes: AGGREGATE ceiling across ALL connected MCP servers + built-in tools in one request (NOT a per-server cap), and conditional on tool search / defer_loading: "Maximum deferred tools: 10,000 tools with defer_loading: true per request". Without defer_loading the binding constraint is the documented 30-50 tool selection cliff plus the context window. Anthropic's own example: a 5-server setup (GitHub, Slack, Sentry, Grafana, Splunk) costs ~55k tokens in definitions before any work; tool search cuts that by over 85%.

tools_mcp.tool_schema_limits_notes: Tools are {name, description, input_schema (JSON Schema)} with optional input_examples, cache_control, strict, defer_loading, allowed_callers and eager_input_streaming. Structured outputs / strict tool use share one documented JSON Schema restriction: pattern (regex) is NOT supported — the Python, TypeScript, Ruby and PHP SDKs strip unsupported keywords and fold them into field descriptions. No documented maximum nesting depth, maximum property count, maximum enum size or maximum total schema size. strict is available on all tools except mcp_toolset; defer_loading is available on all tools (per-tool or per-toolset for MCP). input_examples cost ~20-50 tokens for simple examples and ~100-200 tokens for complex nested objects, and are not available on server tools. Tool definitions can carry cache_control, so a repeated tool array reads at 0.1x input price after a cache write; deferred tools sit outside the system-prompt prefix so defer_loading preserves the cached prefix and composes with strict mode without grammar recompilation. On a 200k window tool definitions are proportionally 5x more expensive than on the 1M models, so defer_loading plus cache_control on the tools array is close to mandatory for multi-server MCP setups. Note the 4,096-token minimum cacheable prompt on this model — small tool arrays may not be cacheable at all.
tools_mcp.other_limits_notes: MCP connector (API layer, beta header mcp-client-2025-11-20; mcp-client-2025-04-04 is deprecated): HTTPS remote servers only over Streamable HTTP or SSE — local stdio servers cannot be attached directly. Of the MCP specification only tool calls are supported; prompts and resources are not. Available on the Claude API, Claude Platform on AWS and Microsoft Foundry (Hosted-on-Anthropic deployments), all in beta. Per-tool mcp_toolset config exposes enabled and defer_loading (default false). Tool search regex variant: max 200-character pattern; error_code values are invalid_tool_input, unavailable, too_many_requests and execution_time_exceeded. Request size 32 MB direct / 20 MB Bedrock / 30 MB Google Cloud. A single request may carry up to 600 images or PDF pages on 1M-window models (100 on 200k-window models). Haiku 4.5 supports tool search / defer_loading, structured outputs / strict tool use, the memory tool, and the automatic context-awareness signals (<budget:token_budget> plus a per-tool-call <system_warning> usage line). It does NOT support task budgets (beta) and is NOT in the programmatic tool calling support list (which requires code_execution_20260120 and covers Fable 5, Mythos 5, Opus 5, Opus 4.8/4.7/4.6/4.5, Sonnet 5/4.6/4.5) — so the ~38% billed-input saving from keeping tool results out of context is unavailable here, which makes defer_loading and client-side result trimming the only levers. A 200k-window model accepts at most 100 images or PDF pages per request (600 on 1M models). Haiku 4.5 supports extended thinking but not adaptive thinking.

strict_function_schema.notes: No OpenAI-style strict function-schema mode that enforces 100-prop / 5-depth / no-oneOf. Anthropic does ship a strict flag (strict:true, plus structured outputs) but its documented rule set is different and looser: the only keyword restriction published is that pattern (regex) is unsupported, and no property-count or depth ceiling is given. Captured in tool_schema_limits_notes.

skills_supported.notes: Agent Skills available on the Claude API, claude.ai, Claude Code (custom Skills only), Claude Platform on AWS and Microsoft Foundry (pre-built Skills require a Hosted-on-Anthropic deployment).

skills_loading_model.notes: Level 1 metadata (name + description from YAML frontmatter, ~100 tokens per Skill) is always in context at startup. Level 2 (SKILL.md body, under 5k tokens) loads only when the Skill triggers. Level 3+ bundled files load only when read; scripts run through bash so only their output enters context. Documented field limits: name max 64 characters (lowercase letters, numbers, hyphens; no XML tags; may not contain "anthropic" or "claude"), description non-empty and max 1024 characters.

skills_context.skills_context_cost_notes: ~100 tokens per installed Skill at startup (Level 1 name+description). When a Skill triggers, its SKILL.md body adds under 5k tokens (Level 2). Level 3 bundled files cost nothing until read; scripts execute through bash so only stdout/stderr enters context. Anthropic states you "can install many Skills without context penalty: until a Skill is triggered, only its name and description occupy context", and documents no numeric ceiling on the number of installed Skills; the binding limit is the context window -- each installed Skill holds its name and description in context, and its full instructions load on invocation.
skills_context.system_prompt_overhead_notes: Tool-use system prompt overhead: 496 tokens (tool_choice auto/none) or 588 tokens (any/tool). Context awareness is active. Note the 4,096-token minimum cacheable prompt length — the highest in the current roster (Opus 5 / Fable 5 / Mythos 5 need only 512) — so short tool arrays and short Skill sets may fall below the caching threshold entirely. System-added tokens are counted but not billed.

prompt_caching.notes: Supported on all active Claude models, automatic and explicit. Multipliers: 5-minute cache write 1.25x base input, 1-hour cache write 2x, cache read (hit) 0.1x. For Claude Haiku 4.5 that is $1.25/MTok (5m write), $2.0/MTok (1h write) and $0.1/MTok (read) against a $1.0/MTok base. Minimum cacheable prompt length: 4,096 tokens. cache_control can be set on tool definitions and on an mcp_toolset, so a stable MCP tool array is cacheable; deferred tools sit outside the cached system-prompt prefix and do not invalidate it.

memory_feature.notes: First-party memory tool (memory_20250818), generally available on the Messages API with no beta header, on "all Claude 4 and later models". Operates as just-in-time retrieval: Claude checks its memory directory and reads files back on demand, so retrieved content enters the window as ordinary input tokens rather than a permanent always-on block. Anthropic does not publish a token accounting rule for memory content.

cached_input_per_mtok_usd.notes: Cache read (hit) = 0.1x base input. 5-minute cache write = 1.25x, 1-hour cache write = 2x.

batch_discount.notes: Message Batches API: $0.5/MTok input, $2.5/MTok output for Claude Haiku 4.5. Batch and prompt-caching discounts stack, and both apply at standard rates across the full context window.

cost.multimodal_billing_notes: Images billed as input tokens at the STANDARD visual-token rate (max 1568 tokens/image); Anthropic's example puts a 1000x1000 image at about $1.30 per thousand images on Haiku 4.5. PDFs the same; audio unsupported. At most 100 images or PDF pages per request on a 200k-window model.

reasoning_billed_as_output.notes: Thinking tokens count toward the context window, count toward rate limits, are a subset of max_tokens, and are billed at the output rate ($5.0/MTok here).

models.notes: Claude Haiku 4.5 (2025-10-15) is unchanged at this refresh and remains Anthropic's fastest, cheapest model — and the only current model with a 200k rather than 1M window, which makes MCP tool-footprint management the binding constraint. WATCH: the deprecations table gives a tentative retirement "not sooner than October 15, 2026", the nearest retirement horizon of any active Claude model, and there is no Haiku 5 as of 2026-08-19. Uses the previous (pre-4.7) tokenizer, so token counts are NOT comparable with Opus 5 / Sonnet 5 / Fable 5 measurements. Strips previous-turn thinking blocks. Supports extended thinking, not adaptive thinking. API model ID claude-haiku-4-5 (alias) or claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 (pinned snapshot).
